# awsappstream_image_permission (Resource)

Manages sharing permissions for a private AppStream image. Image permissions control whether a private image can be used by fleets or image builders in another AWS account. Each permission grants access to **one AWS account** and defines whether the image is usable for fleets, image builders, or both.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "awsappstream_image_permission" "example" {
  name              = "example-image"
  shared_account_id = "123456789012"

  image_permissions {
    allow_fleet         = true
    allow_image_builder = true
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `image_permissions` (Attributes) Defines how the shared AWS account is allowed to use the image. At least one permission must be enabled. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--image_permissions))
- `name` (String) The name of the private AppStream image for which permissions are managed. Changing this value forces the image permission to be replaced.
- `shared_account_id` (String) The 12-digit AWS account ID that is granted permissions to use the image. Each image permission resource manages access for exactly one AWS account.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) A synthetic identifier for the image permission, composed of the image name and the shared AWS account ID. This value is managed by the provider and cannot be set manually.

<a id="nestedatt--image_permissions"></a>
### Nested Schema for `image_permissions`

Required:

- `allow_fleet` (Boolean) Whether the image can be used to create or update AppStream fleets in the shared AWS account.
- `allow_image_builder` (Boolean) Whether the image can be used to create AppStream image builders in the shared AWS account.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import awsappstream_image_permission.example "example-image|123456789012"
```
